_comment: An EXAMPLE design-token file, not a palette to copy. Yours should differ,
and you should be able to say why each value is what it is.
The point of a file like this is that it is the ONE place a color, a
duration, or a spacing step is defined, and all three surfaces read it.
The TUI maps these to the nearest terminal color, the GUI uses them
directly, the matrix uses them as sRGB and gamma-encodes on the way to the
panel. Change 'fault' here and all three change together — that is the
test of whether you really have a system or three lookalike programs.
Check it before you ship:  python3 contrast.py --palette tokens.json
(exits nonzero if any token falls below 3.0:1 against the background)
_surfaces_comment: Every background a foreground token can land on. contrast.py checks each
color against ALL of them and reports the worst case, because that is the
one your operator will actually hit.

non_color_encoding._comment: Every severity must survive a greyscale screenshot.

spacing._comment: One step, everything a multiple of it. 8 is conventional.

type._comment: Two or three sizes, consistently used, read as designed.

motion_ms._comment: Durations in milliseconds. Anything over ~400 on a status change needs defending.
